title: Ninja Five-O
subtitle: A ninja takes the rescue assignment
summary: Ninja Five-O is Hudson Soft's Game Boy Advance action platformer starring Joe Osugi, a ninja confronting terrorists empowered by mysterious masks. Known as Ninja Cop in Europe, it divides the mission between fighting armed opponents and rescuing the hostages held across its stages. A grappling hook gives Joe a way to cross difficult spaces and approach threats from another direction. body: Ninja Five-O is Hudson Soft's Game Boy Advance action platformer starring Joe Osugi, a ninja confronting terrorists empowered by mysterious masks. Known as Ninja Cop in Europe, it divides the mission between fighting armed opponents and rescuing the hostages held across its stages. A grappling hook gives Joe a way to cross difficult spaces and approach threats from another direction. The small handheld levels require attention to both movement and the people being protected, making an effective route something more careful than attacking every figure encountered on the screen.

Joe's grappling hook reaches surfaces above him, allowing a swing or climb to turn a distant ledge into part of the route. The ability supports changes of height and direction that would be unavailable through an ordinary jump. Fighting and rescue take place within the same spaces, so an approach must consider where Joe will land as well as which enemy can be reached. The movement tool gives the player room to plan, offering a way around an immediate threat or a better position from which to continue toward the hostage.

Missions combine several stages with a final boss, placing individual rescue situations inside a larger pursuit of the masked terrorists. Joe's movement and attacks provide different answers to each arrangement of platforms, opponents and captives. The hostage objective gives restraint a practical role in a fast action game, requiring the player to distinguish a person needing help from the threat nearby. Ninja Five-O makes its compact stages memorable through those local arrangements, where the same grappling ability can create a quick escape, a safer attack or the route to somebody still waiting to be saved.
